scope: Cross-city official/public source gap audit for architecture and built-environment milestones in London, New York City, and Belfast, 2008-2026. No candidate events were created.

recommendations.source_name: Planning London Datahub construction lifecycle fields
recommendations.publisher: Greater London Authority and London planning authorities
recommendations.source_family_gap: planning approval rows are present, but commencement and completion lifecycle fields appear under-used
recommendations.license: Public portal and guest API. Existing registry says dataset-level terms should be respected and the London Datastore application dataset does not expose one clear open licence. Retain factual metadata, source URLs, GLA/borough attribution, request parameters, and retrieval dates until reuse terms are confirmed.

coverage_years.note: PLD replaced the London Development Database and is updated during the planning and construction lifecycle.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: The City Hall description says PLD contains planning applications, permissions, commencements, and completions across London planning authorities, so it can turn many existing approval-only rows into staged claims such as documented commencement or final completion when fields are present.
caveats: Do not treat validation, decision, commencement, completion, or opening as interchangeable.
Borough feed quality and backfill completeness vary.
Centroids can be approximate and should not be presented as surveyed site boundaries.
Use existing source IDs instead of creating a duplicate PLD source.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Expand the existing PLD source family and event extraction logic; do not add a second generic London planning application source.

recommendations.source_name: London Development Database planning permissions and completions archive
recommendations.publisher: Greater London Authority
recommendations.source_family_gap: pre-2020 significant development completions and non-residential floorspace/bedroom changes
recommendations.license: UK Open Government Licence (OGL v3) on the London Datastore dataset page.

coverage_years.note: Use for the 2008-2019 slice of this audit window. Housing approvals also extend back to 2000; unit-level approvals are available from 2012 to 2019.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: The archive records significant London planning permissions and includes housing completions, non-residential floorspace, and non-C3 bedroom records. It is especially useful for observed administrative and completion-stage changes before PLD.
caveats: The LDD has been replaced by PLD and is no longer updated.
Coverage is thresholded to significant development, so small works and many civic refurbishments are absent.
Completion rows are administrative monitoring evidence, not opening, occupation, design quality, or outcome evidence.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: The registry already has london-development-database-archive, but it is not represented as an architecture milestone source. Use that ID or canonicalize to it.

recommendations.source_name: Energy Performance of Buildings Certificates open data
recommendations.publisher: UK Government / MHCLG Energy Performance of Buildings Register
recommendations.source_family_gap: post-completion corroboration for new dwellings and non-domestic building use, especially where planning rows do not prove delivery
recommendations.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 for GOV.UK content except where otherwise stated; verify bulk register terms and any address-level restrictions before redistribution.

coverage_years.note: Official statistics cover certificates lodged since Q4 2008; property-level register/open-data availability and fields should be checked before bulk use.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: EPC lodgement dates and new-dwelling/non-domestic certificate records can corroborate that a building or address entered an assessable built/use state after planning approval.
caveats: An EPC is not a construction completion certificate, opening date, or occupation certificate.
Multiple certificates can exist for the same property and data cleaning is needed.
Address-level records need careful privacy and reuse review.
Geometry normally requires address matching or UPRN joins.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Use only as corroboration for delivered built state, not as a replacement for PLD/LDD planning events.

recommendations.source_name: Planning Inspectorate Casework Database and Appeals Casework Portal
recommendations.publisher: Planning Inspectorate / GOV.UK
recommendations.source_family_gap: ordinary appeal decisions beyond called-in and recovered appeal publications
recommendations.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 for GOV.UK content except where otherwise stated.

coverage_years.note: The casework database provides detailed rolling 5-year data plus older 5-10 year anonymized data. The Appeals Casework Portal holds current/recent identifiable cases. It does not provide full 2008-2026 identifiable coverage.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: Appeal outcomes can overturn or confirm local planning decisions and are often the operative administrative milestone for refused or contested architecture schemes.
caveats: Older than 5 years, identifiable fields are removed under retention policy.
Appeal allowed means permission/consent may be granted, not that works started or completed.
Match to local planning references and site addresses before adding any event.
Called-in/recovered decisions are already partly covered.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Do not duplicate mhclg-called-in-decisions; add this only for normal appeal casework not already captured by the called-in/recovered collection.

recommendations.source_name: Planning Data planning-application dataset
recommendations.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
recommendations.source_family_gap: national standard planning application feed for England
recommendations.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 with Crown copyright and database right attribution.

coverage_years.note: The dataset page currently warns that the planning application dataset is incomplete and not ready for use.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: In future, a standardized national application dataset could provide uniform planning application fields and geometry across authorities.
caveats: The dataset page explicitly says it is incomplete and not yet ready for use.
Only a small provider set is currently represented.
For London, PLD is richer and already in the registry.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Reject for current architecture milestone ingestion; monitor later but avoid overlapping PLD London records.

recommendations.source_name: London borough building control application and completion certificate registers
recommendations.publisher: London borough building control services
recommendations.source_family_gap: completion certificate and building-regulations sign-off evidence
recommendations.license: Borough-specific website terms and access rules. Not a unified open data feed.

coverage_years.note: Coverage varies sharply by borough, portal, retention period, and whether the works used local authority building control or a registered/private approver.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: A completion certificate is strong evidence that inspected works reached building-control completion for a specific address or application.
caveats: No central London bulk open dataset was identified.
Many boroughs charge for copies, require property-owner/solicitor requests, or retain only limited public metadata.
Private registered building control approver records may sit outside the borough record.
Use for targeted corroboration only.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Do not build a bulk ingest around fragmented borough completion-certificate pages until a lawful, repeatable access path is specified.

recommendations.source_name: Building Safety Regulator higher-risk building control approval application data
recommendations.publisher: Health and Safety Executive / Building Safety Regulator
recommendations.source_family_gap: post-2023 higher-risk building control gateway evidence for tall residential, hospitals, and care homes
recommendations.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 for GOV.UK content except where otherwise stated.

coverage_years.note: BSR became the building control authority for higher-risk buildings in England on 2023-10-01. Current releases are management information, not a mature project-level city feed.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: Could eventually corroborate gateway/building-control approval milestones for higher-risk London buildings after 2023.
caveats: Current releases are largely aggregate management information and may not expose reusable project-level identifiers, addresses, or geometry.
Gateway approval is not construction completion or occupation.
Coverage starts too late to cover most of the 2008-2026 window.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Track as a future corroboration family, not an event source now.

recommendations.source_name: NYC Capital Projects Dashboard and Capital Projects Database (CPDB)
recommendations.publisher: NYC Mayor's Office of Operations / NYC Department of City Planning via NYC Open Data
recommendations.source_family_gap: citywide public capital construction stages outside Parks-only tracker and agency press pages
recommendations.license: NYC Open Data / NYC.gov terms. NYC Open Data policy says public datasets are made available without license requirement or usage restrictions except limited cases; retain NYC attribution and dataset metadata.

coverage_years.note: Current CPDB records include project date fields and current versions; historical BYTES of the BIG APPLE releases should be archived per run for stable snapshots.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: The dashboard covers City construction projects including buildings and provides current phase, projected completion, budget, and agency schedule details. CPDB point/polygon data adds FMS/project IDs and geometry for many public capital investments.
caveats: Current phase or projected completion is not final completion unless the row states actual completion or completed status.
Some projects are infrastructure or equipment, not architecture; filter to buildings, public realm, schools, cultural facilities, libraries, housing, and station/site works.
Open Data rows need version snapshots because dashboard releases update over time.
Not all projects have precise locations.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Use CPDB as the citywide capital spine; keep Parks tracker, DDC pages, SCA pages, and NYCHA pages as corroborating agency-specific evidence.

recommendations.source_name: NYC Public Design Commission design reviews, meetings, and archive
recommendations.publisher: NYC Public Design Commission
recommendations.source_family_gap: official design-approval milestones for city-owned buildings, public spaces, bridges, art, streetscape elements, parks, and memorials
recommendations.license: NYC.gov terms; treat meeting packets, agendas, and archival records as official public records but avoid republishing long text/images unless rights are checked.

coverage_years.note: The archive spans far earlier than 2008; current design review pages and meeting materials cover contemporary project submissions.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: PDC has jurisdiction over permanent structures, landscape architecture, art, and streetscape elements on or over city-owned property. Approvals can document conceptual, preliminary, final, and post-approval design milestones for public works.
caveats: Design approval is not construction start, completion, opening, or operational performance.
Scraping PDF packets may be needed; record meeting date, action, submitting agency, site, and project title.
Some archive materials may have image or third-party rights constraints.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Use PDC only for public design review milestones; do not duplicate agency press releases that already document opening or completion.

recommendations.source_name: NYC DOT Current Projects and older street improvement project pages
recommendations.publisher: NYC Department of Transportation
recommendations.source_family_gap: street, plaza, corridor, bus-priority, pedestrian, bike, and public-realm design/proposal/completion evidence
recommendations.license: NYC.gov terms; use factual project metadata and source URLs unless a specific Open Data resource is used.

coverage_years.note: The current projects page links older project pages from 2007 through 2025 and current 2026 material.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: NYC DOT pages and presentation PDFs document street improvement projects, public plazas, greenways, bus bulbs, curb extensions, and other physical public-realm changes with project extents and meeting dates.
caveats: Proposal, community-board presentation, installation, and capital reconstruction phases must be separated.
Many pages contain design intent and safety rationale; do not claim outcome effects.
PDF maps may require manual geometry extraction and rights-aware citation.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Do not mix DOT public-realm project pages with traffic-count datasets; they answer different evidence questions.

recommendations.source_name: NYCHA Capital Projects and Needs Tracker
recommendations.publisher: New York City Housing Authority
recommendations.source_family_gap: public housing renovation, modernization, building systems, grounds, facades, elevators, resilience, and safety projects
recommendations.license: NYC.gov terms; tracker data is public-facing but should be snapshotted with attribution and source URL. Check tracker-specific terms before bulk redistribution.

coverage_years.note: NYCHA describes planned, ongoing, or completed projects since 2017 in the enhanced tracker.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: The tracker provides project scope, phase timelines, progress, budgets, locations within developments, and architect/engineering or contractor information for public housing capital works.
caveats: Tracker progress updates can change; store retrieval date and page snapshot metadata.
A planned project is not an observed physical change.
Project scopes can be building systems rather than visible architecture; label accordingly.
Development-level location is not always a building footprint.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Use tracker records for NYCHA capital works and press pages for named announcements/openings.

recommendations.source_name: NYC School Construction Authority Capital Plan Reports and Data
recommendations.publisher: New York City School Construction Authority
recommendations.source_family_gap: school construction, additions, capacity projects, capital improvement, healthy schools, and mandated works beyond isolated factsheets
recommendations.license: NYCSCA site terms/copyright. Use factual metadata, source URLs, document titles, project names, dates, and retrieval dates unless reuse rights are confirmed.

coverage_years.note: The page exposes current and prior capital plan reports, including FY2020-2024 and FY2025-2029 project/process documents. Use the 2010-2026 portion for this audit.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: SCA reports monitor school projects through completion and list capacity projects in design or construction, seats gained/lost, and school capital plan categories.
caveats: Capital plan inclusion is not completion.
Many records are planning or funding records; corroborate openings with SCA/DOE press or school pages.
Some site rendering or PDF content may carry separate rights.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Use SCA reports to find candidate school projects, then de-duplicate against existing SCA factsheet/opening source IDs.

recommendations.source_name: MTA Capital Program Dashboard and construction project pages
recommendations.publisher: Metropolitan Transportation Authority
recommendations.source_family_gap: station accessibility, subway/LIRR/Metro-North station rebuilds, entrances, elevators, and transit architecture capital works
recommendations.license: MTA data and website terms are source-specific. Preserve MTA attribution, project page URL, and access date; verify terms before bulk reuse of dashboard data.

coverage_years.note: Capital program plans span multiple 5-year periods. Current dashboards are strongest for active and recent project progress.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: MTA capital pages can document station accessibility projects, reconstructed entrances, new elevators, and major station facility work with agency status and delivery milestones.
caveats: Transit feed/ridership APIs do not prove physical station changes.
Capital plan inclusion is not construction or completion.
Project boundaries may cover packages across many stations.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Separate MTA capital project evidence from existing MTA operational/ridership feeds.

recommendations.source_name: NYC DOB permit, filing, and certificate datasets
recommendations.publisher: NYC Department of Buildings via NYC Open Data
recommendations.source_family_gap: none for this round; already heavily represented
recommendations.license: NYC Open Data / NYC.gov terms.

coverage_years.note: Existing registry and milestone corpus already use these datasets heavily.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: DOB filings, permits, and certificates can support administrative construction, alteration, demolition, and occupancy milestones, but this is already a core NYC source family in the corpus.
caveats: Permits are administrative authorization, not completed work.
Job filings and permit issuance can duplicate the same underlying work if not keyed carefully.
Avoid another broad DOB scrape unless it fills a clearly named subfamily such as demolition permits or final certificates.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Reject as a new recommendation because it would duplicate existing high-volume NYC source IDs.

recommendations.source_name: Northern Ireland Planning Portal public register records
recommendations.publisher: Northern Ireland Planning Portal / Belfast City Council / planning authorities
recommendations.source_family_gap: application-level planning records and decision notices beyond committee minutes and selected monthly lists
recommendations.license: Planning Portal public-register terms. Existing registry recommends factual metadata and source URLs pending fuller reuse review.

coverage_years.note: Use Belfast records in the 2008-2026 window; portal-level completeness and document availability vary by case and period.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: The register is the official per-application source for validation dates, descriptions, site addresses, decision statuses, decision dates/notices, application references, and linked documents.
caveats: Validation/application/advertisement/committee/decision dates are not construction or completion dates.
Older document attachments may be incomplete or unavailable.
No bulk API was confirmed in this audit; extraction may require careful portal interaction and rate limits.
Use application references to de-duplicate against committee and monthly decision PDFs.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Expand the existing ni-planning-portal-public-register source rather than creating another Belfast planning portal ID.

recommendations.source_name: Planning Appeals Commission Northern Ireland appeal search and decisions
recommendations.publisher: Planning Appeals Commission / Northern Ireland Courts and Tribunals Service support body
recommendations.source_family_gap: appeal outcomes after Belfast planning decisions and DfI referred cases
recommendations.license: PAC website terms not confirmed as an open bulk licence. Use factual appeal metadata, decision URLs, and attribution; check document reuse terms before copying decision text.

coverage_years.note: The site provides appeal search, recent decisions, and decision documents; historical search coverage should be tested before claiming completeness.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: PAC decides appeals against council planning decisions and handles hearings/reports on cases referred by departments, so it can fill gaps where a refusal, condition, enforcement, listed-building, advertisement, or other consent outcome later changed on appeal.
caveats: Appeal allowed/refused is an administrative outcome, not physical works.
Decision reports may contain personal data or copyrighted third-party submitted drawings.
Need application-reference matching against Belfast council/NI Planning Portal records.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Use PAC only for appeal/referred-case decisions, not to duplicate original council planning decisions.

recommendations.source_name: OpenDataNI / DfC Historic Environment Division ESRI REST and heritage spatial datasets
recommendations.publisher: Department for Communities Historic Environment Division via OpenDataNI / Spatial NI
recommendations.source_family_gap: canonical heritage geometry/status datasets beyond hand-curated HED pages and committee notifications
recommendations.license: UK Open Government Licence (OGL) for the listed buildings dataset and many HED OpenDataNI resources; verify per resource. OpenDataNI portal states data is under OGL.

coverage_years.note: Listed Buildings Northern Ireland was created as an OpenDataNI resource in 2016 and is updated monthly; underlying statutory records predate the resource.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: Provides authoritative heritage status and coordinates for listed buildings, scheduled monument areas, industrial heritage, HED consultation zones, and related built-heritage records that can contextualize or corroborate designation/status events.
caveats: A heritage asset point/status is not a physical alteration event.
Listed-building points are centre points of designated areas, not surveyed building footprints.
Designation dates may require HED/nidirect detail pages or committee notification records.
Do not duplicate existing HED source IDs without canonicalization.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Use OpenDataNI as the canonical spatial/status feed and keep existing HED page IDs as detail-page citations.

recommendations.source_name: Investment Strategy for Northern Ireland Investment Pipeline and project pages
recommendations.publisher: Northern Ireland Executive / Strategic Investment Board
recommendations.source_family_gap: public-sector capital project status for transport, schools, health, housing, public realm, and other infrastructure
recommendations.license: ISNI/SIB website terms should be checked before redistribution. Use factual project metadata, URLs, dates, and attribution while retaining source snapshots.

coverage_years.note: Current pipeline reports planned, build/delivery, and completed projects; historical 2008-2010 coverage is weak and should not be assumed.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: The pipeline is searchable by project/contract and reports project status in build and delivery phases, including completed projects. It can identify official public-sector milestones that are not visible in local planning records.
caveats: Pipeline project status is not a site completion/opening unless explicitly stated.
Some entries are regional or programme-level rather than Belfast site-level.
Need to filter to built-environment projects and attach planning/press/department evidence for dates.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Use ISNI as a discovery and status spine for public capital projects; retain department/source-specific pages as final evidence.

recommendations.source_name: Department for Communities public realm, environmental improvement, and Belfast Regeneration pages
recommendations.publisher: Department for Communities Northern Ireland
recommendations.source_family_gap: public-realm starts, completions, masterplans, regeneration frameworks, and streetscape works
recommendations.license: Crown copyright material on the Department for Communities site is reusable under Open Government Licence terms unless otherwise indicated; preserve attribution and avoid third-party media/logos.

coverage_years.note: Pages and publications span the full audit window, but each scheme needs source-specific dates.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: DfC pages document public realm and environmental improvement schemes in Belfast city centre and greater Belfast, including route extents, funding, consultation, start dates, due completion dates, and sometimes completion statements.
caveats: Masterplans and consultations are not delivered physical change.
Do not infer economic, safety, or regeneration outcomes from scheme intent text.
Many pages provide corridor descriptions rather than reusable GIS geometry.
Separate scheme consultation, start, completion, and post-completion maintenance records.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Use DfC regeneration/public-realm pages as the official source family for public realm; do not bury them under belfast-architecture-public-pages catch-all IDs.

recommendations.source_name: Department of Education NI major works and school building project pages
recommendations.publisher: Department of Education Northern Ireland / Education Authority / ISNI
recommendations.source_family_gap: school construction starts, openings, extensions, refurbishments, and major capital programme stages
recommendations.license: Northern Ireland Crown copyright / Open Government Licence unless otherwise indicated; preserve departmental attribution and avoid media reuse without review.

coverage_years.note: Department news and major works references cover multiple school projects in the audit period; ISNI provides database cross-reference for major works.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: Department pages define major capital works as new buildings, rationalisation/amalgamation new builds, extensions, and refurbishments, and news pages often state start, opening, completion, contractor, and investment facts.
caveats: Planning/design approval, sod-cutting, construction start, completion, and official opening are separate events.
Some projects are outside Belfast; filter by city boundary and school address.
Do not claim educational outcomes from building investment pages.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Use Department of Education as canonical publisher for school capital works rather than generic public-page catch-all IDs.

recommendations.source_name: Belfast Region City Deal project pages and annual reports
recommendations.publisher: Belfast Region City Deal partnership / Belfast City Council and partners
recommendations.source_family_gap: major cross-agency capital projects, tourism/regeneration, innovation campuses, transport links, and public facilities from 2021 onward
recommendations.license: Official partnership website; factual metadata and URLs should be retained pending fuller reuse review. Partner pages may have separate terms.

coverage_years.note: The deal was formally signed in this period and project pages/annual reports cover current delivery stages.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: Project pages identify named capital projects, locations, lead partners, status, funding agreements, business-case stages, and sometimes design-team/procurement milestones for Belfast-area built-environment changes.
caveats: BRCD project pages often describe future benefits and intended outcomes; do not convert those into observed change claims.
Some projects are outside Belfast city.
Business-case or funding-stage milestones are not physical starts or completions.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Create or use a BRCD family only for deal/project-level milestones; keep project-specific departmental pages for construction/opening evidence.

recommendations.source_name: Belfast City Council Building Control records and completion/inspection services
recommendations.publisher: Belfast City Council
recommendations.source_family_gap: building-regulations inspection and completion evidence
recommendations.license: Belfast City Council website copyright/terms. No open bulk data licence identified for building-control records.

coverage_years.note: Service page is current; historical searchable bulk coverage was not identified.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: If accessible for a specific application, inspection/completion records would strongly corroborate that building works reached a regulatory completion stage.
caveats: The public page is service guidance, not a bulk register.
Building control records may include personal, commercial, or restricted material.
Council building control may not hold private approver records.
Targeted evidence requests are not suitable for a repeatable open atlas ingest.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Reject as a bulk source for this round; revisit only if Belfast publishes an open register or a documented access workflow.

recommendations.source_name: Belfast Crane Survey and private market construction reports
recommendations.publisher: Private consultancies / market reports
recommendations.source_family_gap: independent built-completion survey style evidence
recommendations.license: Private report terms; not an official/public open data source for repository ingestion unless explicit reuse permission is obtained.

coverage_years.note: Approximate coverage based on known survey families; not verified as an ingest source here.

recommendations.why_it_can_support_observed_architecture: Market construction surveys can be useful discovery material for completions and starts, but they are not official administrative evidence.
caveats: Private methodology and licensing may block redistribution.
Survey categories may aggregate buildings and omit source rows needed for provenance.
Use only as a lead to official planning, building, or public agency records.
recommendations.duplicate_avoidance_note: Do not ingest private survey rows into the official/public source registry without explicit licence review.
